fields.text: A vision model writes your face card - the numbered anchors that make you recognisably you, with your current hair on its own line as the one thing allowed to change. An LLM stylist picks one haircut that suits your face and your brief, and its plan may not drop a single anchor; a second LLM compresses the plan into a surgical edit instruction, and Muse Edit renders the new cut on the original photo. Then the loop closes: a second vision read inventories only the features visible in the preview, a GLM auditor scores the card against that read-back anchor by anchor - kept, changed, lost - plus whether the hair actually changed, and a Decide judge labels the preview same person new cut, face drifted, barely a haircut or different person. Four model families, and the editor does not get to grade its own likeness. See recipes/haircut-preview.md.

nodes.name: Haircut preview, identity-checked - read the face, plan the cut, render, audit

fields.text: I want a change: noticeably shorter and easier to manage, still professional for office work. Keep my natural colour and waves - no dye, no straightening. Nothing that hides my face.

fields.q: You are the identity clerk in a haircut-preview pipeline. Look at this portrait photo and write a FACE CARD in this exact shape: a first line 'Sitter:' with your best guess at age range and presentation, plus the clothing and setting you can see; then a numbered list of 5 to 8 FACE ANCHORS - the features that make this person recognisable as themselves and must NOT change in a haircut preview: face shape, eye colour and shape, eyebrows, nose, lips, skin tone, freckles or moles with their side and position, ears, and any glasses or facial hair. Then a line 'Current hair:' describing colour, length and where it ends, texture, parting and any fringe - this is the one part that is allowed to change. Then a last line 'Vibe:' with two or three words for the mood the expression suggests. List ONLY what you can actually see; if you are unsure of an anchor, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. No haircut suggestions, no styling advice.

nodes.name: Face card - Gemini reads the sitter

fields.system: You are a hair stylist planning ONE haircut preview. The input gives a haircut brief first, then the sitter's face card: a sitter line, a numbered list of face anchors, a current-hair line, and a vibe line. Write ONE plan in this exact shape: a title line naming ONE specific haircut, chosen because it suits this face shape and the brief (say why in a few words on the same line); a 'Keep exactly:' line that repeats every numbered face anchor, shortened if needed but never dropped or altered; then a 'New hair:' list of 3 to 5 concrete choices - the new length and where it ends, layers or their absence, parting, fringe or none, and the finish. The brief's hard constraints win over everything: if it forbids dye or straightening, colour and texture stay exactly as the card describes them. No change of face, skin, clothing or background is allowed. Output the plan only, no preamble.

You write ONE edit instruction for an image editor, from a haircut plan. The editor receives the original portrait photo. Your instruction must: start with 'Keep exactly:' followed by the plan's face anchors in compressed form; then describe the new hair concretely (length and where it ends, layers, parting, fringe, finish, colour and texture unchanged if the plan says so); end with 'Same person, same face, same clothes and background, photorealistic, no other people, no text.' Keep it under 110 words. Output the instruction only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Preview - Muse Edit cuts the hair

fields.question: The text is a sitter's face card: a numbered list of face anchors that make this person recognisable, plus a current-hair line. The image is a haircut preview that claims to show that same person with a new, noticeably shorter haircut. Which verdict fits? 'same person, new cut' means the preview carries the listed face anchors - face shape, eyes, nose, lips, freckles or moles on the correct sides - AND the hair is clearly a new, shorter style. 'face drifted' means it is plausibly the same person and the hair changed, but one or two listed anchors moved, changed or vanished. 'barely a haircut' means the face is intact but the hair is much the same length and style as the card describes. 'different person' means the preview contradicts the card on face shape or several anchors. Judge the face anchors and the hair change, not the photo's beauty.
fields.options:
same person, new cut
face drifted
barely a haircut
different person

fields.q: You are the preview reader in a haircut-preview pipeline. Look at this portrait and list ONLY what you can actually see, one per line: face shape, eye colour and shape, eyebrows, nose, lips, skin tone, freckles or moles with their side and position, ears, and any glasses or facial hair. End with one line starting 'Hair:' describing the hair as you see it - colour, length and where it ends, texture, parting and any fringe. Do not guess at anything hidden or cropped out - if you are unsure of a feature, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any other picture; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Preview read-back - Gemini reads the preview

fields.system: You are an identity auditor. The input gives a sitter's face card - a sitter line, a numbered list of face anchors, a current-hair line and a vibe line - then the marker 'PREVIEW READ-BACK:' and a reader's inventory of the features visible in a haircut preview. Compare the two, numbered anchor by numbered anchor. Output one line per numbered face anchor, in card order, starting 'KEPT - ' if a matching feature is visible in the preview, 'CHANGED - ' if the feature is there but its colour, side or shape differs, or 'LOST - ' if it cannot be found, followed by the anchor's short name. Ignore the sitter and vibe lines. Then one line starting 'Hair:' saying how the preview's hair, per the read-back's Hair line, differs from the card's current-hair line - or that it barely differs. End with one line 'Summary: X of Y face anchors kept.' Judge by the read-back text only, not by what a preview ought to show. Output the audit only, no preamble.
